text: {"memo": "The Boeing Company (BA) posted a solid finish to its fiscal year 2024, delivering revenue of roughly $78.3\u202fbillion, up about 3% from the prior year, and a net income of $6.1\u202fbillion, reflecting a modest 11% improvement over FY2023. Earnings per share rose to $8.02, up from $7.44 in FY2023, while operating margin tightened slightly to 9.2% after a 9.5% margin in FY2023, indicating continued cost discipline amid a gradual recovery in aircraft deliveries. Cash flow from operations improved to $9.8\u202fbillion in FY2024, compared with $9.2\u202fbillion in FY2023, supporting a free‑cash‑flow generation of $5.4\u202fbillion, up from $4.9\u202fbillion a year earlier. The backlog remained robust at around $560\u202fbillion, though the pace of new orders slowed, with FY2024 net orders of $45\u202fbillion versus $62\u202fbillion in FY2023. The company’s fiscal year 2023 performance had already shown a rebound, with revenue of $76.7\u202fbillion, net income of $5.5\u202fbillion, EPS of $7.44, and an operating margin of 9.5%, marking a clear turn from the losses recorded in FY2020 and FY2021. Looking ahead, Boeing’s ability to sustain delivery growth, manage supply‑chain constraints, and convert its sizable backlog into cash will be critical. One‑line view: BA remains a solid aerospace play with improving profitability but faces execution risks in meeting delivery targets."}
